note: Swappable grammar pack (R46, §9.3/§9.11) for the email line. Machine-checked wall between namespaces: 'decision' strings appear while the player decides or loses (labels, terms, refusals, alerts, status rungs) and stay SOBER per §9.3 clauses 2-3; 'flavour' carries the recognition comedy for quiet surfaces. Authenticity law for this line (§9.3/§9.11): the drama is the OPERATOR's — the smudged postmark, the form nobody reads, the list the customer is proud of — never the spam itself. No payloads, commands, tool names-as-how-to, or technique instruction anywhere; abuse exists only as complaint, listing notice, provider silence, and consequence.

nodeId.desc: Board object the decision surface is about (pool / server id).

availableAtTick.desc: Tick at which the queued intent or a freed hand presents.

providerDomain.desc: A major mailbox provider holding one of the four postmarks.

domainName.desc: A customer sending domain under placement review.

placementPct.desc: Inbox placement rate — the fifth-axis metric for this line (§0.3).

volumeMsgs.desc: Message count in an outbound burst or rate-limit verdict.

accountName.desc: The sending account (compromised, eager, or legitimate-bulk).

listName.desc: The blocklist that opened a listing against your space.

prefix.desc: Your address block cited in a listing or upstream notice.

responseHours.desc: Hours the desk allows before a listing hardens or a case ages.

hour.desc: Clock hour a ticket or burst was filed/observed at.

minute.desc: Clock minute a ticket or burst was filed/observed at.

day.desc: Day of the warm-up or the quarter, for the intern's log.

poolName.desc: The quarantine pool holding a risky sender.

decision.type.mail-hosting.name: The Post Office
decision.type.mail-hosting.codex: The deliverability line: your currency is IP reputation, held by other people, appreciating slowly and destroyable by one tenant in an hour. The defense points outward, the meter is four postmarks that smudge independently, and you can be perfect and still be blocked.
decision.goal.mail-hosting.binding: Your server accepted it. That is not the same sentence as 'they received it.'
decision.scarce.mail-hosting.qos: Transactional mail outranks bulk, and bulk outranks nothing that outranks a delisting appeal — the invoice email that misses is worth more than the two hundred spams that make it.
decision.skin.mail-hosting.inspector: Sorting hall cutaway — envelopes on conveyor belts, the pulped-grey torrent in the side chute, four postmarks above the doors, and the hall's cleanliness is the number.
decision.cac.mail-hosting.todo: (CAC and time-to-profit unpriced for this line — §6.6 Companion B costs only the shared-web affiliate channel; email prices its load as abuse-desk budget per customer, not acquisition. Placeholder until §6.6 Companion B prices the email channel; see bundle _todo.)
decision.verbs.mail-hosting.transfer.1: some resources are held by third parties and cannot be bought back.
decision.relations.mail-hosting.mastery: Placement reads the hall: pools are warmed before the quarter, not during it, and the forms get answered faster when your postmarks are crisp.
decision.relations.mail-hosting.distillate: Playbook: reputation is a balance-sheet asset — defend it like capital, reconcile it like a ledger, and never let the desk mailbox go unread.
decision.handover.mail-hosting.runs-out: Your IP reputation. It appreciates over months and one customer can spend all of it in an hour.
decision.handover.mail-hosting.kills-you: A compromised mailbox at 2am, four hundred thousand messages, and a listing nobody will explain.
decision.handover.mail-hosting.customer-wants: Their mail reaches the inbox. Not the junk folder, not a bounce — the inbox.
decision.rosetta.mail-hosting.warmup: The IP warm-up ramp is the oversell ratio played backwards: volume is earned from the providers, not sold to the customers.
decision.rosetta.mail-hosting.rates: Per-account outbound rate limits are cgroup caging pointed the other way — the same dial, now aimed at what leaves.
decision.scenarios.mail-hosting.backscatter: Bounce messages from forged senders flood your queues: the workload is entirely refusal receipts for mail that was never yours, and every hour of it is pool capacity nobody paid for.
decision.scenarios.mail-hosting.joe-job: Someone sends from a domain you never owned with your address on the mail — a forgery engineered to look legitimate, priced in your postmarks, defended with paperwork.
decision.scenarios.mail-hosting.mail-only-custome: Tiny revenue, outsized risk: the mail-only customer is the single most abuse-prone account you can sign, and one compromised mailbox spends your whole outbound reputation.
decision.alert.postmark-smudge: Placement at {providerDomain} reading {placementPct} for {domainName}. No error was returned. Nobody is going to tell you why. The postmark is crisp and stamped in slightly the wrong place.
decision.terms.rate-limit: Per-account outbound rate limits hold {accountName} under the volume your pool has warmed through — legitimate bulk senders will call this exactly the interference it is.
decision.terms.delist-form: Delisting is answered, not appealed: {listName} case {caseId} reopens on evidence completeness, first response inside {responseHours}.
decision.refusal.hands-exhausted: Both hands are committed. The {verb} intent is queued and presents when a hand frees at tick {availableAtTick}.
decision.refusal.stamped-in-future: The {verb} intent is stamped for tick {availableAtTick}, ahead of the current minute. Nothing was spent.
decision.refusal.unknown-node: No board object named {nodeId} exists at the current tick. Nothing was changed.
decision.refusal.edge-exists: A {relationKind} cable already links {nodeId} to those endpoints. The existing edge was left as it is.
decision.refusal.slot-occupied: {slotName} on {nodeId} is occupied. One supplier per socket; disconnect before you reconnect.
decision.status.rung-5: We are aware of the fire.

flavour.ticket.subject.reset-in-spam: my customers' password resets are landing in spam
flavour.ticket.body.reset-in-spam: The reset links and the receipts are in their junk folders, three days late, and the accounts are now locked. Your servers report healthy. Fix what you are actually selling.
flavour.ticket.subject.list-bought: I bought a mailing list, when can we send?
flavour.ticket.body.list-bought: Forty thousand addresses, 'legally acquired', filed at {hour}:{minute}. The customer is cheerful. The warm-up plan says no. The contract says complicated.
flavour.ticket.subject.angry-bulk: your rate limit is costing me sales
flavour.ticket.body.angry-bulk: {accountName} sends every invoice at five on Friday and the per-account outbound cap says no. They are a legitimate bulk sender, and they are correct that the cap is the problem tonight.
flavour.ticket.subject.warmup-impatient: why is my new pool sending so slowly
flavour.ticket.body.warmup-impatient: Day {day} of the ramp and the customer wants full volume now. The ramp is the product this month, and the proof they can see is the postmark smudging while they wait.
flavour.abuse.canon.listing: From: {listName} — a listing has opened against {prefix}. Traffic attributed to your address space. Delisting begins with the form; the form begins with the evidence.
flavour.abuse.canon.postmaster: Postmaster correspondence from {providerDomain}: volume accepted, engagement poor, placement degraded. No policy citation. No appeal channel. Read the smudge, not the words.
flavour.abuse.canon.sudden-volume: Desk notice: {accountName} sent {volumeMsgs} in the first hour of an account that existed one hour ago. Signup vetting was skipped to protect the conversion funnel. The invoice arrives; the reputation bill was already paid.
flavour.press.headline.delist: {hostName} delisted from {listName} after {responseHours} of silence; statement calls the listing 'a false positive we respect'.
flavour.press.headline.greeting-season: Greeting-card volume forecasts up this quarter; independent senders advised to warm early. Analysts decline to comment on postmarks.
flavour.forum.thread.placement: Anyone else's mail landing in junk at {providerDomain} this week?
flavour.forum.thread.blame: {hostName} says the listing is 'resolved'. Tell that to my password resets.
flavour.chatter.desk.stack: The abuse@ mailbox has 6,000 unread messages. That is not a backlog. That is the reason.
flavour.chatter.hall.clean: The hall is spotless, the postmarks are crisp, and the mail is still arriving in the wrong folder. Perfect and still blocked.
flavour.codex.snowshoe: The snowshoe spammer steps lightly across every provider at once — each postmark smudges a little, never all together, and no single alert ever fires.
flavour.codex.quiet-column: Deliverability churn is the quiet column of the ledger: customers leave for reasons the player will not see on any latency graph.
flavour.loading.tip.outbound: This is the level where the defense points outward. You are filtering what leaves.
flavour.loading.tip.cold-space: Cold IP space is a promise, not an asset: you have not earned volume against it yet.
flavour.intern.entry.postmarks: Day {day}: learned the meter is four separate opinions, and the quietest postmark is the loudest problem.
flavour.sticky.note.ptr: reverse DNS was subtly wrong for months. It was discovered in one afternoon. We check it first now.
flavour.vendor.reply.firmware: Have you tried updating to the latest firmware?
flavour.vendor.reply.log-bundle: Please collect a full log bundle.
flavour.vendor.reply.known-issue: This is a known issue, fixed in the next release (no ETA).
flavour.achievement.fine-at-one: Fine at One, Blocked at the Others.
flavour.achievement.six-thousand: Six Thousand Unread: Root Cause Found.
flavour.canary.quarantine-pool: {accountName} routes through quarantine pool {poolName} for {responseHours} before general release. The clean pools hold where they are until this one reads green.
